# Live-provider parity

Status: Foundation landed; no live capture has run
Last reviewed: 2026-07-26

This report compares mockOS against a real Entra or Okta tenant. It is advisory:
it never blocks a release. A case with no live capture is recorded as
`not-captured`, which is **not** a pass — absent evidence must never read as
present evidence.

## Divergence ledger

Every difference a live run finds must resolve to an entry here. An unledgered
difference is reported as a defect. An entry with `intentional: false` is a known
bug that is tracked but not yet fixed, and still reports as a defect.

| Id | Provider | Case | Field | Intentional | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `D-01` | okta | `*` | `requestBody.passCode*` | yes | The software TOTP factor accepts only the static synthetic passcode 000000. RFC 6238 time steps, drift, enrollment, and shared secrets are not implemented. |
| `D-02` | okta | `*` | `responseBody.access_token.__jwt.payload.acr` | yes | Tokens issued after the factor and session bridge keep acr urn:okta:loa:1fa:any. mockOS does not model MFA assurance elevation. |
| `D-02b` | okta | `*` | `responseBody.id_token.__jwt.payload.amr` | yes | The ID token always carries amr [pwd] regardless of the factor path taken. |
| `D-03` | entra | `*` | `responseBody.id_token.__jwt.payload.tid` | yes | Tenant identifiers are derived deterministically from the environment seed so runs are reproducible. A real tenant id is assigned by the provider. |
| `D-04` | entra | `entra-discovery` | `responseBody.userinfo_endpoint` | yes | UserInfo is deliberately omitted from discovery until an executable route exists, rather than advertised and unimplemented. |
| `D-04b` | okta | `okta-discovery` | `responseBody.userinfo_endpoint` | yes | UserInfo is deliberately omitted from discovery until an executable route exists. |
| `D-07` | entra | `entra-device-create` | `responseBody.verification_uri_complete` | yes | The Entra device policy omits verification_uri_complete by design; Okta includes it. |
| `D-15` | entra | `*` | `responseBody.id_token.__jwt.payload._claim_sources*` | yes | Group overage emits a claim source at 201 groups with a 1000-id fallback ceiling. Real Entra thresholds and endpoints differ. |
| `D-19` | entra | `*` | `responseBody.error_description` | yes | Error descriptions, trace and correlation identifiers, and timestamp formatting are synthesised. The OAuth error code is the comparable field, not the prose. |
| `D-19b` | okta | `*` | `responseBody.errorSummary` | yes | Okta error summaries and errorId values are synthesised; errorCode is the comparable field. |
| `D-26` | entra | `*` | `responseBody.access_token.__jwt.payload.token_use` | no | mockOS emits a token_use claim on Entra tokens. Real Entra v2 tokens have no such claim. Not yet fixed. |
| `D-27` | entra | `*` | `responseBody.access_token.__jwt.payload.aud` | no | The Entra access token uses client_id as its audience and carries the full ID-token claim set. Real Entra scopes the audience to the resource API. Not yet fixed. |
| `D-28` | entra | `entra-discovery` | `responseBody.subject_types_supported*` | no | Discovery advertises pairwise subject types while sub equals oid equals the user id, which is public, not pairwise. Not yet fixed. |
| `D-29` | okta | `okta-discovery` | `responseBody.response_modes_supported*` | no | Discovery advertises query-only response modes while the HTTP adapter accepts and implements form_post. Not yet fixed. |
| `D-30` | okta | `*` | `responseBody.access_token.__jwt.payload.aud` | no | The Okta access token uses client_id as its audience. A real custom authorization server uses its own audience, typically api://default. Not yet fixed. |
| `D-31` | okta | `*` | `responseBody.id_token.__jwt.payload.groups*` | yes | The Okta groups claim carries display names while Entra carries identifiers. Both are deliberate and provider-shaped. |
| `D-34` | entra | `*` | `status` | no | The authorize endpoint requires openid in scope. Real Entra permits resource-only scopes, so a resource-only authorize request diverges. Not yet fixed. |
| `D-35` | entra | `entra-discovery` | `responseBody.cloud_instance_name` | yes | Discovery constants cloud_instance_name and tenant_region_scope are fixed synthetic values. |
| `D-36` | okta | `*` | `responseHeaders.x-rate-limit-limit` | yes | Rate-limit headers are fixed synthetic constants rather than a real quota. |
| `D-37` | entra | `*` | `responseHeaders.location` | yes | Hosted login is mockOS-branded with no session cookie, so every authorize re-prompts. prompt, max_age, acr_values, and domain_hint are ignored. |
| `D-39` | okta | `okta-authn-factor-verify` | `responseBody.errorCode` | no | A non-numeric passCode is rejected at the HTTP layer with E0000001 before the factor comparison, where real Okta returns E0000068. Not yet fixed. |
| `D-40` | okta | `okta-revoke` | `responseHeaders.content-type` | yes | Revocation returns 200 with a null body and no content-type. |
| `D-41` | entra | `*` | `responseBody.id_token.__jwt.payload.ver` | yes | Entra emits the string "2.0" and Okta the number 1. Both are deliberate and provider-shaped; assert the exact type. |
| `D-43` | entra | `entra-device-create` | `responseBody.user_code` | yes | The device user code is eight characters from a custom alphabet, matching neither provider's real format. |
| `D-44` | entra | `*` | `responseBody.timestamp` | yes | The Entra error timestamp renders ISO 8601 with the T replaced by a space and the Z retained. |

## Out of scope

mockOS does not implement these, so they bound the parity claim:

- client_credentials
- on-behalf-of and token exchange
- resource owner password credentials
- implicit and hybrid response types
- PKCE plain
- pushed authorization requests and request objects
- DPoP and mTLS sender-constrained tokens
- UserInfo
- RP-initiated logout
- session cookies and silent SSO
- dynamic client registration
- SAML and WS-Federation
- consent screens
- multi-tenant common, organizations, and consumers authorities
- Conditional Access and risk evaluation
- Okta IDX and Sign-In Widget
- factor enrollment and non-TOTP factor types
- Okta administrative APIs
